pieces.h: Exam Details
pieces.t: The Virginia Department of Professional and Occupational Regulation Board for Contractors regulates individual tradesmen in electrical, plumbing, HVAC, gas fitting, and other trades. For Virginia tradesman licensing exams, candidates apply for eligibility through the Board before testing, and PSI administers the examination program. The exam is administered by computer, with one question displayed at a time and a score report provided after the exam. The Virginia Journeyman Electrician exam is a trade licensing exam designed to confirm that candidates have the minimum required knowledge of electrical principles, practices, statutes, and regulations. Electrical exam preparation should include both code-based review and practical trade knowledge. Candidates should be ready for questions involving NEC application, electrical theory, wiring and protection, wiring methods, conductors, grounding and bonding, equipment, motors, calculations, and safe installation practices.

pieces.h: Open Book Test
pieces.t: The Virginia tradesman examination rules allow candidates to bring reference books. Study guides and sample examinations are not allowed in the exam room. Reference books may be highlighted, underlined, and indexed before the exam, but they must otherwise be unmarked and not written in. This makes preparation with the correct reference material and clean code navigation habits especially important. Open-book testing does not mean the exam is easy. It means candidates must know how to locate information quickly, understand what the question is asking, and apply the correct rule under time pressure. A candidate who has not practiced with the code book may spend too much time searching and not enough time answering. The National Electrical Code 2026 Paperback with Tabs included in this combo helps students practice finding articles, tables, definitions, exceptions, and common electrical rules before exam day. pieces.h: Licensing Steps
pieces.t: Virginia journeyman electrician candidates begin by reviewing the current tradesman application instructions and confirming that their education and work experience meet the Board for Contractors requirements. The Board approves applications for testing, and candidates must receive eligibility before scheduling the exam. Eligibility is issued through the licensing process and is used when registering for the examination. A practical path begins with gathering experience documentation, training records, and any required application materials. Candidates then submit the Virginia tradesman exam and license application for the electrical classification. After the Board approves the application, the candidate registers for the examination through PSI and selects an available testing option. PSI provides computer-based testing procedures, score reporting, and scheduling support. After passing the exam, candidates complete the remaining licensing steps required by Virginia.

pieces.h: State Requirements
pieces.t: Virginia regulates individual tradesmen through the Department of Professional and Occupational Regulation Board for Contractors. Electrical tradesmen must hold the appropriate credential before performing regulated electrical work in the Commonwealth. The state’s tradesman licensing structure includes electrical licensing, and candidates must satisfy the Board’s education, experience, application, examination, and licensing requirements. Virginia’s tradesman application process requires candidates to use the correct application for individuals seeking electrical, plumbing, HVAC, or gas fitting licensure. The application process is separate from business contractor licensing. A journeyman electrician candidate should focus on the individual tradesman license requirements, not a contractor business license, unless they are also pursuing a separate contractor license for a business entity. pieces.h: Test Information and Study Materials
pieces.t: A strong study plan should include scheduled review time, repeated NEC lookup practice, calculation drills, and question review. Candidates should avoid relying only on memorization. pieces.h: State Requirements
pieces.t: Virginia uses a state-level tradesman licensing structure through DPOR and the Board for Contractors. The state regulates journeyman and master tradesman credentials, including electrician classifications. Candidates preparing for a Virginia Master Electrician license should follow the state licensing process rather than a local-only license path. The Virginia Master Electrician credential is an advanced individual license for experienced electrical professionals. Candidates pursuing this credential should be ready to demonstrate strong technical knowledge, code understanding, calculation ability, safety awareness, and knowledge of the responsibilities that come with advanced electrical licensing. Virginia also has contractor licensing requirements for businesses that offer, bid, contract, or perform construction and trade work. Individual licensing and contractor licensing are not the same thing. An individual master electrician license shows that the person has met the state requirements for that trade level, while a contractor license applies to the business activity.
